question: Does the packed browser receipt SDK reduce diagnostic-envelope authoring or maintenance across equivalent markup/framework drift compared with a strong generic host implementation?
nonClaim: This experiment never assesses task correctness. Every arm receipt must say taskOutcome NOT_ASSESSED; a changed:true postcondition PASS is only a receipt-local observation and may never be counted as task success.

comparison.H: A strong clean-room host helper that generically discovers roles, accessible names, state, content, centre-point coverage, and opaque regions, then emits a versioned receipt-shaped envelope.
comparison.R: The npm-packed and temporarily installed @zumer/snapdom-receipt package, called through createBaseline and createReceipt.
fairness: H may use roles, accessible names, DOM APIs, computed layout/hit testing, and generic reusable JavaScript.
No arm may use variant IDs, fixture oracle markers, or per-variant selectors/configuration.
Both arms observe the same root before and after the same fixture mutation.
A generic H helper that handles every variant with zero variant-specific edits eliminates any demonstrated maintenance advantage; that outcome must be reported.
Fixture construction, the independent oracle, and result scoring are test infrastructure and are excluded from integration LOC for both arms. Their exclusion must be disclosed.

families: typed status-content change keyed by role and accessible name
became-covered actionability change keyed by role and accessible name
current unobservable-region source type and exact count
auditedTelemetry.exactness: For each arm and trial, the canonical set for these four families must equal the independent oracle set: no missing and no unexpected facts within the audited families. Other valid receipt facts such as geometry, additions, removals, or became-visible entries are retained as evidence but excluded from this preregistered fact-set comparison.
auditedTelemetry.oracle: A separate primitive reader uses data-oracle markers only in test fixtures, reads raw ARIA/DOM state, status text, elementFromPoint coverage, and canvas count, and never calls either arm or reads either arm output.

variants.action: button / Approve account / pressed false to true
variants.status: status / Approval result / Ready to Approved

variants.drift: nested wrappers and a div-backed ARIA button/status
variants.action: button / Approve account / pressed false to true
variants.status: status / Approval result / Ready to Approved

variants.drift: framework-style node remount without stable DOM IDs; role and accessible name remain stable
variants.action: button / Approve account / pressed false to true
variants.status: status / Approval result / Ready to Approved

variants.drift: product copy and live-region role legitimately change
variants.action: button / Authorize account / pressed false to true
variants.status: alert / Authorization result / Ready to Approved

variants.drift: control becomes a switch with checked state and the live region becomes a log
variants.action: switch / Automatic approval / checked false to true

schedule.readerOrder: balanced by variantIndex plus repetition parity before the mutation; finish order reverses baseline order
schedule.pageReset: fresh local page for every paired trial
schedule.browserRuns: one execution of the complete runner after every static gate passes

metrics.telemetryExactness: exact canonical fact sets versus the independent oracle, by arm and variant
metrics.initialAuthoringLOC: physical nonblank, non-comment lines inside preregistered marker-delimited host-generic and SDK-integration blocks in the runner; braces and declarations count
metrics.variantMaintenanceLOC: arm runtime references to a specific variant or arm-specific variant adapter/configuration; expected zero only if source gates confirm no variant IDs occur inside either runtime block
metrics.predicates: four shared telemetry families, generic postconditions, task predicates, and any additional predicates/configuration per variant
metrics.schemaStability: required envelope paths present, stable contract/version/taskOutcome, and one envelope-shape hash per arm across all variants; item-level optional-shape variation is reported separately
metrics.evidenceBytes: UTF-8 bytes of the exact JSON-safe post receipt and the local baseline, with SHA-256 retained
metrics.wallTime: browser-side baseline, post, and cycle elapsed milliseconds, descriptive only

staticGatesBeforeBrowser: preregistration and runner paths are distinct; the result path does not exist
runner parses and the checked-in browser SDK distribution is fresh
SDK is npm-packed and installed offline into a temporary directory with dev dependencies omitted
installed SDK declares no runtime dependency fields and its bundle hash matches its manifest
both arm runtime blocks contain none of the five preregistered variant IDs
source LOC markers are unique and metric definitions can be computed
fixture and oracle declarations cover all five variants and all four audited fact families
browserAndCleanupGates: Chromium uses a dedicated temporary persistent profile; personal Chrome state is never opened
the fixture binds only 127.0.0.1 on an operating-system-assigned port and rejects port 8377
all browser network requests remain on the fixture origin or blob/data URLs
all 15 paired trials complete once per arm and the oracle validates every declared transition
all receipts have taskOutcome NOT_ASSESSED; postcondition PASS is never a task-success metric
browser context closes, loopback server closes and refuses a new connection, and the temporary directory/profile is removed before any result is written
any cleanup failure fails the run closed

decisionRule.maintenanceReductionSupported: Only if R is at least as telemetry-exact as H and requires fewer variant-specific adapter LOC or predicates on at least one drift variant.
decisionRule.maintenanceReductionNotDemonstrated: If a single reusable H helper is exact across all variants with the same zero variant-specific LOC/predicates as R, report no demonstrated maintenance advantage, regardless of initial implementation size.
decisionRule.initialAuthoringOnly: If both arms tie on maintenance but the SDK integration block is smaller than the clean-room H generic engine, report only a one-time buy-versus-build authoring reduction, conditional on the host not already owning an equivalent helper.
decisionRule.schemaClaim: Schema advantage is supported only if R is stable and H is not; if both are stable, report a tie.
decisionRule.correctnessAndCommercialClaims: Task correctness, end-to-end success, production generalization, demand, and willingness to pay are NOT ASSESSED under every outcome.
